correctness.rationale: For sorted three-positive incomes with sum S, G=2(c-a)/(3S) and A_1=1−3(abc)^(1/3)/S; thus strict opposite rankings iff (R_x−R_y)(P_x−P_y)>0. With two incomes of gap d, product=(S²−d²)/4, hence same weak ordering. Independently enumerated every sorted positive integer triple and pair at each S=3,…,11 with integer products and exact rational ranges: no strict reversals for S≤10; S=11 one unordered pair (1,5,5),(2,2,7), products 25<28 while ranges4<5. At S=9 (1,4,4),(2,2,5) tie in range 3, products16 vs20, first weak-order split. Enumeration proves only bounded threshold; the analytic reductions are exact.
residual_risks: Independent finite tests cannot alone prove infinite quantified claims; analytic premises and structural lemmas reconstructed.
